title: Proposal cards with dry-run apply and immutable audit ledger for batching/caching recommendations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Ship a new Console Optimize experience that surfaces independent, actionable ‘proposal cards’ for batching and KV-cache recommendations, lets operators run a dry-run (simulated apply) to preview diffs and estimated cost/latency impact, and records every apply/rollback in an immutable audit ledger tied to user identity and PRs. This ticket covers the product spec, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and handoffs to design and engineering. The experience must prioritize safety: all automated changes are optional, dry-runs must be non-destructive, and automatic rollbacks must be simple and auditable. Links: Confluence spec (https://confluence.redwood.ai/optimize/proposal-cards-dryrun), mockups (https://drive.redwood.ai/optimize/mockups/proposal-cards-v2.png)
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a compact ‘proposal card’ per recommendation with score, expected token/cost delta, and confidence band.
Each proposal card exposes a ‘Dry-run’ action that computes a simulated diff of runtime config changes and provides an estimated cost and P90 latency delta without applying changes to production.
Dry-run results include a machine-readable diff (+ human diff view), a preview of per-route token breakouts, and potential rollback instructions if applied.
Apply workflow requires explicit acknowledgement and creates an immutable audit entry with user, timestamp, input prompt set, and generated diff + optional linked GitHub PR.

An Apply History view surfaces chronological entries with expand/collapse details, ability to tag entries (investigate/monitor), and a single-click rollback that performs a dry-run first and then applies revert if approved.
All UI actions generate events for telemetry (recommendation_shown, dryrun_requested, dryrun_completed, apply_requested, apply_completed, rollback_requested, rollback_completed).
Security/compliance review logged and signed-off for data retention and KMS usage prior to GA release.
tasks: PM: Finalize spec and priority list of recommendation types (batch size, cache TTL, cache scope) and test prompts.
Design: Deliver proposal card visuals, diff UI (side-by-side and inline), and compact apply history table (2 iterations).
Eng (backend): Implement dry-run simulator endpoint that computes deterministic diffs and cost/latency estimates based on historical traces.
Eng (frontend): Implement card components, diff preview modal, and apply history page with pagination and filters.
Eng (infra): Add immutable ledger storage backed by append-only log (S3+WAL) and wire auth identity into audit entries.
QA: Define regression tests for dry-run safety, simulate concurrent apply/rollback scenarios, and validate telemetry events.
Docs: Write Console help center article and internal runbook for rollback/playback procedures.
SRE: Run a canary with 5 pilot customers and monitor cost/latency and rollback rates for 2 weeks.
notes: Tradeoffs: Tight coupling between dry-run estimator and runtime traces increases accuracy but adds maintenance burden. Initially support heuristics for new model families and augment with trace-based calibration.
Fallbacks: If simulator fails or confidence < 60%, UI should surface a warning and disable one-click apply, forcing manual review.
Privacy: Dry-run must redact customer prompt contents from audit view unless user explicitly opts in for full payload retention.
Rollout: Feature flag per-org + admin-only by default; open to all orgs after 2-week pilot and safety metrics OK.
Compliance: Audit ledger retention policy must be configurable per-tenant (90/365/ever) and integrate with KMS for key rotation.
qa_plan: Scenario A: Dry-run on a high-throughput route returns expected token/cost delta and zero runtime changes; verify no config mutated.
Scenario B: Apply proposal for cache TTL change while another apply is in-flight; verify optimistic locks and clear error to user.
Scenario C: Rollback via UI produces a dry-run of revert, shows expected deltas, and completes revert; verify audit entry links to original apply.
Scenario D: Simulate failed dry-run estimator and confirm UI disables apply and surfaces strong warning.
Scenario E: Audit entries immutable — attempt to modify entry via API should be rejected; confirm CRC/hash integrity.
metrics: % of recommendations converted to applied configs (target 20% for pilot)
Median cost savings per applied recommendation (USD/month)
False-positive rate where applied change causes >5% latency regression (target <2%)
Dry-run estimator success rate and average latency (target <2s for interactive flows)
Telemetry event coverage for all UI actions (100%)
